meta.prompt: Initial extraction from als-concepts-from-experience.md, als-design-decisions.md, als-tooling-gaps.md

items.title: Sub-Delamains do not exist
items.summary: Scaffolded a 'chapters' Delamain as a sub-flow of the main 'launch' Delamain — ALS has no such concept.
items.rule: A Delamain is triggered by a delamain-typed field on an entity. No parent-child relationships. One entity + one concern = one Delamain with inlined states.

items.title: Spec HITL gates ≠ Delamain operator gates
items.summary: Translated all 7 spec UI touchpoints into Delamain operator gates — only genuine human decisions need gates.
items.rule: Ask: 'Can an agent make this decision reliably?' If yes, no gate needed. Agent-to-agent handoffs require no operator state.

items.title: authoring.ts path must be absolute in standalone projects
items.summary: Copied a relative path from the ALS reference system that only works inside the ALS monorepo — fails in standalone projects.
items.rule: Standalone projects must use the absolute installed path: /Users/<user>/.claude/plugins/cache/als-marketplace/als/<version>/alsc/compiler/src/authoring/index.ts

items.title: Title source fields must be non-null
items.summary: Used a nullable field (internal_label) in the entity title template — compiler error PAL-CV-SHAPE-001.
items.rule: Any field referenced in a document title source must have allow_null: false. Put optional fields in the body, not the title.

items.title: provider is required on all agent states
items.summary: Left out 'provider: anthropic' on every agent state — compiler caught all of them.
items.rule: Every state with actor: agent must declare provider. Valid values: 'anthropic', 'openai'. There is no default.

items.title: session-field is required on resumable states
items.summary: Marked states resumable: true without providing the session-field name for recovery.
items.rule: resumable: true requires session-field: '<name>'. This field is implicitly added to entity frontmatter at runtime — does not need to be in the entity fields block.

items.title: System root for alsc is the project root, not .als
items.summary: Passed .als as the system root argument — compiler looked for .als/.als/system.ts (double path).
items.rule: The system-root argument is . (project root). The compiler appends .als/system.ts itself.

items.title: The compiler is the source of truth, not the skills
items.summary: /als:init and the compiler are known to be unaligned in 0.1.0-beta.28.
items.rule: If alsc validate passes, the scaffold is correct regardless of what /als:init would generate. Use the compiler as the arbiter.

items.title: The dispatcher is commit-driven, not CLI-driven
items.summary: Expected a command to advance a Delamain step-by-step — the dispatcher polls git HEAD for committed state changes.
items.rule: Commit a state change → dispatcher sees it on next poll (30s) → invokes the agent → auto-commits result. No manual trigger.

items.title: Deploy and bootup are separate operations
items.summary: Assumed running bootup would also compile and deploy the module — they are two distinct steps.
items.rule: alsc deploy claude . projects .als/ to .claude/. /als:bootup starts dispatchers. Neither does both. No skill exists for deploy (filed: nfrith/als#2).

items.title: Hook-centric fan-out
items.summary: Nick's diagram had thumbnail deriving from title — we made both title and thumbnail derive from hook.
items.rule: Hook is the framing angle. Both title (text) and thumbnail (visual) express the same hook independently. Deriving thumbnail from title creates redundancy and weaker CTR.

items.title: 4 operator gates (not 7 from spec, not 3 from first design)
items.summary: Iterated from 7 spec gates → 3 (too few, missed chapters) → 4 (correct).
items.rule: Gates are: awaiting-input, awaiting-hook-selection, awaiting-chapter-review, awaiting-review. All other transitions are agent-to-agent.

items.title: Chapters inlined into launch Delamain
items.summary: Originally a separate chapters Delamain — dropped and inlined as 3 states after Nick pointed out it was orphaned.
items.rule: One entity + chapter processing as part of main flow = inline. Use a second Delamain field only if the concern is genuinely parallel and independent.

items.title: Analysis = 12 parallel agent prompts, no gate
items.summary: Ran 12 parallel sub-agent prompts for analysis — purely extractive, no human judgment needed.
items.rule: Analysis feeds hook generation. All 12 results land in ANALYSIS section. Made resumable because 12 parallel agents is long-running.

items.title: Chapter timing = tool call, not workflow state
items.summary: Timing adjustment is mechanical (index + arithmetic) — doesn't need AI reasoning or a Delamain state.
items.rule: The Delamain models decisions, not tools. External fine-tuning tool runs out-of-band during awaiting-chapter-review gate.

items.title: internal_label nullable, excluded from title template
items.summary: internal_label is optional annotation — excluded from title template because compiler requires non-null title sources.
items.rule: Title source = project_code only. Always non-null, always unique. internal_label stays in entity body as optional metadata.

items.title: Module named fli-launch (not youtube-launch-optimizer)
items.summary: AWB already has a module called youtube-launch-optimizer — used fli-launch to namespace to FliLaunch.
items.rule: Namespace modules to the product they belong to. Avoids collision and makes skill IDs (fli-launch-manage, fli-launch-pipeline) unambiguous.

items.title: Two skills: manage + pipeline
items.summary: Split into fli-launch-manage (CRUD) and fli-launch-pipeline (operator console) — separate administration from operation.
items.rule: Manage = session lifecycle (create, list, inspect, cancel). Pipeline = workflow operation (advance, rework at human gates). Follows ALS reference system conventions.

items.title: FliHub as transcript source (not direct file reference)
items.summary: Agent calls FliHub API with project_code rather than reading filesystem paths directly.
items.rule: FliHub is the canonical video project management system. It normalizes data and provides a consistent API. Agents shouldn't need filesystem knowledge.

items.title: No /als:deploy skill
items.summary: After authoring a module, there is no skill to project .als/ to .claude/ — must run the compiler command manually.
items.rule: Filed as nfrith/als#2. Workaround: bun /path/alsc/compiler/src/cli.ts deploy claude .

items.title: /als:init and compiler not aligned
items.summary: /als:init generates a different scaffold shape than what the compiler validates as correct.
items.rule: Known pre-release gap, confirmed by Nick. Use compiler as source of truth. Scaffold manually if /als:init output fails validation.

items.title: No sub-Delamain concept — underdocumented constraint
items.summary: Operators from nested workflow systems expect child workflows — ALS has no such concept, and it's not prominently documented.
items.rule: Should add to ALS docs: 'No sub-Delamain concept. Inline states or add a second delamain-typed field on the entity.'

items.title: Compiler error output is JSON, not human-readable
items.summary: Running alsc validate directly produces structured JSON with error codes — requires parsing to understand.
items.rule: Use /als:validate skill which interprets errors in readable form, or pipe to jq.

items.title: No session seeding skill or template
items.summary: Creating the first entity record requires the module's manage skill — no generic scaffold or template generator.
items.rule: Use /fli-launch-manage → Create. The manage skill handles record creation with correct frontmatter.

items.title: authoring.ts absolute path not documented for standalone projects
items.summary: Reference system examples use a monorepo-relative path that fails in standalone projects — not documented anywhere.
items.rule: ALS install docs should explicitly note standalone projects need the absolute installed path in authoring.ts.
